# Diagnostic Settings Coverage

Read-only. Pick **subscriptions**, then **resource groups**, and this workbook lists the resources in that scope **with and without diagnostic settings**.

Inventory comes from Azure Resource Graph (ARG). Diagnostic settings come from **live Azure Resource Manager (ARM) reads, one read per selected resource**. Azure Resource Graph has no diagnostic settings table, so there is no way to answer this without reading each resource. No logs, no keys, no configuration changes, no backend, no deployment.

## Step 0 - choose the scope

Keep the scope small. Every resource left in **Resources to check** costs one live ARM request each time this page runs.

If **Step 1** shows a request error instead of a table, narrow **Resource types**: many Azure resource types do not support diagnostic settings at all, and reading one of those can fail the whole batch.

parameters.name: Subscriptions
parameters.label: Subscriptions
parameters.description: Select explicit subscriptions. The ARG source supports at most 1,000 subscriptions per query.

parameters.name: ResourceGroups
parameters.label: Resource groups
parameters.query:
ResourceContainers
| where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions/resourcegroups'
| project value = tolower(id), label = strcat(name, '  |  ', subscriptionId), selected = false
| order by label asc
| take 1000
parameters.description: Values are full resource group IDs, so identical names in different subscriptions stay distinct. There is deliberately no default: choosing All across many subscriptions can queue thousands of ARM reads. Recheck this after changing subscriptions.

parameters.name: ResourceTypes
parameters.label: Resource types
parameters.query:
Resources
| extend ResourceGroupId = tolower(strcat('/subscriptions/', subscriptionId, '/resourceGroups/', resourceGroup))
| where '*' in ({ResourceGroups}) or ResourceGroupId in~ ({ResourceGroups})
| summarize Count = count() by type
| project value = tolower(type), label = strcat(type, '  (', Count, ')')
| order by label asc
| take 1000
parameters.description: Narrow to the types you care about. Many Azure resource types do not support diagnostic settings at all; reading those wastes requests and can surface errors.

parameters.name: Resources
parameters.label: Resources to check (one ARM read each)
parameters.query:
Resources
| extend ResourceGroupId = tolower(strcat('/subscriptions/', subscriptionId, '/resourceGroups/', resourceGroup))
| where '*' in ({ResourceGroups}) or ResourceGroupId in~ ({ResourceGroups})
| where '*' in ({ResourceTypes}) or tolower(type) in~ ({ResourceTypes})
| project value = id, label = strcat(name, '  |  ', type)
| order by label asc
| take 1000
parameters.description: Defaults to every resource matching the filters above. Deselect resources to reduce live ARM requests. The dropdown itself returns at most 1,000 items.

content.json:
## Step 1 - the two live sources

These are the raw reads that Step 2 combines. They stay visible on purpose: **this is where request errors appear**. If either panel shows an error, Step 2 is incomplete and must not be read as 'not configured'.

content.query:
Resources
| extend ResourceGroupId = tolower(strcat('/subscriptions/', subscriptionId, '/resourceGroups/', resourceGroup))
| where '*' in ({ResourceGroups}) or ResourceGroupId in~ ({ResourceGroups})
| where '*' in ({ResourceTypes}) or tolower(type) in~ ({ResourceTypes})
| where id in~ ({Resources})
| project Name = name, Type = type, ResourceGroup = resourceGroup, SubscriptionId = subscriptionId, Location = location, ResourceId = id
| order by Type asc, Name asc
| take 1000
content.title: Source A - resource inventory from Azure Resource Graph (up to 1,000 rows)
content.noDataMessage: No resources returned for the selected scope.

content.title: Source B - live diagnostic settings from ARM (one read per selected resource)
content.noDataMessage: No diagnostic settings returned for any selected resource.

content.json:
## Step 2 - coverage for the selected scope

Source A joined to Source B. One row per resource, plus one row per diagnostic setting found on it. Use the column filter on **Diagnostic settings** to split the list.

`No setting returned` means this workbook received **no diagnostic setting rows** for that resource. That happens when the resource genuinely has none, **and also** when the read failed, was denied, was throttled, or the type does not support diagnostic settings. Check Step 1 for errors and confirm in Step 3 before treating a resource as unconfigured.

## Step 3 - authoritative detail for one resource

Select a row in the Step 2 grid. Only this section performs a dedicated, paged read for a single target, so **use it to confirm anything the bulk lists suggest**.

To inspect a service child that Azure Resource Graph does not list as its own resource, add its suffix below. Example: for a storage account's Blob service, enter `/blobServices/default`. A parent storage account and its Blob service are different targets with different settings.

parameters.name: ChildPath
parameters.label: Optional child suffix

paramValidationRules.message: Leave empty, or enter type/name pairs only, such as /blobServices/default. No URL, whitespace, encoded characters, query string, fragment, or trailing slash.

parameters.description: Appended to the selected resource ID for the two panels below only. Leave empty to inspect the resource itself.

content.json:
**Exact ARM target being read:**

`{SelectedResource}{ChildPath}`

This target does not change when the Step 0 filters change. If you narrow the scope after selecting a row, the selection can stay behind - re-select a row, and always check the target above. The two panels below are separate live reads, not one atomic snapshot. A 403, 404, 429, or any other request failure is an **error**, not an empty result, an unsupported resource, or a compliance verdict.

content.title: All diagnostic settings on the exact target, with their entries and destinations

content.json:
**Reading settings:** one row is one diagnostic setting. Click **LogEntries** or **MetricEntries** to expand every JSON entry; `enabled: true` and `enabled: false` are preserved, as are `category` and `categoryGroup`. Click **Setting** for row details including the full destination identifiers, or scroll the grid horizontally. Entries belong only to the destinations on the same row. An absent optional array or field means the API did not supply it; it is not proof that the resource is unsupported. `logAnalyticsDestinationType` is the API value, for example `Dedicated`, not an inferred mode.

An empty-success message applies only to its own completed request. Do not interpret results while either panel is loading or showing an error.

content.json:
## What this workbook cannot tell you

**`No setting returned` is not a compliance verdict.** A resource appears there when the ARM read returned an empty collection **or** when that read failed, was denied by RBAC, was throttled, or the resource type does not support diagnostic settings. The bulk read makes one ARM request per resource, and a resource whose request fails contributes no rows, exactly like a resource with no settings. Confirm individual resources in Step 3, and watch the Step 1 ARM panel for errors.

**Matching is by resource ID string.** Bulk rows are attributed to a resource by stripping the `/providers/microsoft.insights/diagnosticSettings/...` suffix from each setting ID. If ARM returns the resource ID with different casing than Azure Resource Graph stored it, that resource can show as `No setting returned` even though Step 3 shows settings. Step 3 is authoritative.

**Request volume.** Every selected resource costs one ARM request on every run and refresh. Narrow by resource type and deselect resources you do not need. Many resource types do not support diagnostic settings at all, and one failing read can fail the whole batch panel.

**Coverage, not correctness.** Compare each setting's log `category` with the live **Category** names in Step 3, and check `categoryGroup` entries against **CategoryGroups**. Compare metric entries only with **Metrics** categories. **Available does not mean recommended**; this workbook does not recommend `allLogs` and does not evaluate a baseline. Metric export through diagnostic settings is different from resource logs and from metrics in Metrics Explorer; not every metric or dimension is exportable. Configuration metadata does not prove data is arriving at a destination. Log contents, destination contents, and keys are never read.

**Scope limits.** Azure Resource Graph is RBAC-filtered and eventually consistent, returns at most 1,000 rows here, and dropdowns hold at most 1,000 items; a row limit is not a completeness guarantee. Service children such as `blobServices/default` are not listed by Azure Resource Graph, so they never appear in the bulk lists - use the child suffix in Step 3. There is no estate-wide total, production classification, compliance score, recommendation, history, or remediation, and no Azure Resource Graph table of diagnostic settings exists to build one from.

**Access.** Viewers need read access to the underlying resources as well as to the workbook; sharing a workbook grants neither. Saving the workbook is your own separate Azure action and needs workbook write permission in a resource group you are allowed to use. No Azure tenant was accessed while building this workbook; local checks are not a substitute for trying it in the portal.
